title: Buy American AAdvantage Miles For 50% Off (1.88 Cents Each): Worth It?
summary: American AAdvantage is selling miles at up to 50% off through December 2, 2026, working out to 1.88 cents each if you buy 500,000. Here's when buying makes sense.
content: American Airlines is currently offering a rare elevated promotion on purchasing AAdvantage miles. Through December 2, 2026, AAdvantage members can purchase miles with up to a 50% discount, which is potentially an opportunity to buy miles for 1.88 cents each. While that’s not a price at which I’d proactively pick up miles, there are definitely some situations where that could represent a good value, if you have an immediate use in mind, especially for first and business class travel. Note that offers like this are extremely rare — while American offers a 40% off promotion on buying miles consistently, the 50% off promotion seems to come around just once or twice per year. Link: Buy American Airlines AAdvantage miles with a discount Buy American Airlines miles with a promotion Between 12:01AM CT on November 27 and 11:59PM CT on December 2, 2026, American AAdvantage is offering up to a 50% discount (or 100% bonus, if you prefer) on buying miles . The offer is tiered, and you get a bigger discount the more miles you buy, as follows: Buy 1,000-2,000 miles, receive no discount Buy 3,000-9,000 miles, receive 10% off Buy 10,000-29,000 miles, receive 20% off Buy 30,000-89,000 miles, receive 30% off Buy 90,000-150,000 miles, receive 40% off Buy 151,000-499,000 miles, receive 45% off Buy 500,000 miles, receive 50% off As you can see, you need to buy a lot of miles to get the best price! Buy American AAdvantage miles for 50% off How much does it cost to buy American Airlines miles? Ordinarily American sells AAdvantage miles for 3.5 cents each pre-tax, or 3.76 cents after factoring in the 7.5% federal excise tax. That’s before any discounts or bonuses. In this case if you max out the promotion and buy 500,000 AAdvantage miles, you’d pay a total of $9,406.25, which comes out to 1.88 cents per mile (that factors in the 7.5% tax). Keep in mind that American Airlines mileage purchases are non-refundable, and buying AAdvantage miles doesn’t count toward your Loyalty Points total (other than any amount you may spend on an eligible credit card). Purchased miles typically post nearly instantly, but in some cases, it can take up to four hours for them to post. Buy American AAdvantage miles for 1.88 cents each The 50% discount is the best price we’ve seen from American AAdvantage in recent years, and again, it only comes around once or twice per year. With the standard 40% off promotion on buying miles, you’d ordinarily pay 2.26 cents per mile. How many American Airlines miles can you buy? The American AAdvantage program ordinarily allows members to buy at most 300,000 miles per account per calendar year, before factoring in any bonuses. However, during this promotion, that cap has been increased to 500,000 miles. AAdvantage accounts less than 30 days old aren’t eligible to buy American Airlines miles. Miles can only be purchased in 1,000-point increments. Redeem AAdvantage miles for Cathay Pacific business class How do you buy American Airlines miles? The process of buying American Airlines miles is easy — the easiest way is to simply follow this link . Alternatively, you can go to aa.com, click on “AAdvantage” at the top of the page, and then click on “Buy, gift or transfer miles.” From there, you’ll be prompted to log into your AAdvantage account, and then that’s where you can select how many miles you’d like to buy. When you buy American Airlines miles, they’ll typically post to your account instantly. Can you buy American Airlines miles? Yes, you absolutely can buy American Airlines miles, you just have to be aware of a few restrictions. For one, your account needs to be at least 30 days old. On top of that, you have to stay within the annual cap. It’s possible to buy miles for yourself or others, but you’ll need to be sure you use the right account to make the purchase. Is this a good deal? At 1.88 cents per mile, the current promotion is 50% below the standard price. That matches the best deal we’ve tracked. Unlike Delta SkyMiles and United MileagePlus, American AAdvantage continues to publish award charts for travel on partner airlines, and redemption rates are largely quite good, especially for travel in premium cabins on partner airlines. Among the “big three” carriers in the US, I tend to think AAdvantage has the best redemption opportunities. I find the cost of business class redemptions to be excellent in many cases. There are instances where it could make sense to pick up miles during a promotion with a short term use in mind. Just to give a few examples of some of my favorite uses of AAdvantage miles (all redemption rates are one-way): For 57,500 miles you can fly from the United States to Morocco in Royal Air Maroc business class For 60,000 miles you could fly from the United States to Japan in Japan Airlines business class For 70,000 miles you could fly from the United States to most of Asia in Cathay Pacific business class For 70,000 miles you can fly from the United States to India in Etihad business class For 75,000 miles you can fly from the United States to South Africa in Qatar Airways business class Now, unfortunately the catch is that partner award availability is in many instances quite limited. For airlines like Cathay Pacific, Etihad, and Qatar Airways, the airlines now largely restrict premium awards to members of their own frequent flyer programs. So definitely do your research before buying any miles. Another thing worth mentioning is that if you redeem for travel on British Airways, get ready to pay huge carrier imposed surcharges , which could be hundreds of dollars on a long haul premium cabin trip. So that wouldn’t be my preferred use of American Airlines miles. Redeem AAdvantage miles for Qatar Airways business class What airlines can you redeem American Airlines miles with? American Airlines belongs to the oneworld alliance, so you can redeem AAdvantage miles on all oneworld airlines. On top of that, you can redeem miles on some of American’s other partner airlines, including Aer Lingus, Air Tahiti Nui, China Southern, Etihad Airways, and GOL Airlines, among others. Redeem AAdvantage miles for Air Tahiti Nui business class How much are American Airlines miles worth? Everyone will value mileage currencies differently, and based on my latest miles & points valuations , I consider AAdvantage miles to be worth 1.5 cents each. However, I tend to value points pretty conservatively, and there are many ways to get way more value from AAdvantage miles than that. Do American Airlines miles expire? American AAdvantage miles don’t expire as long as you have at least some account activity once every 24 months . Eligible activity includes earning or redeeming AAdvantage miles in any quantity. What other ways can you earn American Airlines miles? There are lots of great ways to earn American miles aside from outright buying them: There are excellent welcome bonuses on co-branded American AAdvantage credit cards You can convert Citi ThankYou points into American AAdvantage miles at a 1:1 ratio, and can also transfer Marriott Bonvoy points into American AAdvantage miles at a 3:1 ratio, with 5,000 bonus airline miles for every 60,000 Bonvoy points transferred You can earn AAdvantage miles with a Bask Savings Account You can earn AAdvantage miles for everyday purchases with programs like AAdvantage Dining and SimplyMiles Redeem AAdvantage miles for Royal Air Maroc business class American Airlines buy miles promotion FAQs Is American currently offering a promotion on buying miles? How does the American Airlines tiered discount for buying miles promotion work? The offer is tiered, and you get a bigger discount the more miles you buy. What's the best promotion American has offered on buying miles? The best promotion I’ve seen from American in the past couple of years is for a 50% discount, which would get you a price of 1.88 cents per mile, after taxes. However, that promotion only seems to come around once or twice per year. Otherwise, the program has a 40% off promotion. How many American Airlines miles can you buy? The American AAdvantage program ordinarily allows members to buy at most 300,000 miles per account per calendar year, before factoring in any bonuses. However, in some cases that cap on buying miles is increased. Miles can only be purchased in 1,000-point increments. Can you buy American Airlines miles? Yes, you absolutely can buy American Airlines miles, you just have to be aware of a few restrictions. For one, your account needs to be at least 30 days old. On top of that, you have to stay within the annual cap. Bottom line Through December 2, 2026, American AAdvantage is offering a discount on buying miles. The program is offering up to a 50% discount when you buy American Airlines miles, which is an opportunity to buy them for 1.88 cents each. While I wouldn’t speculatively buy miles at this cost, with a specific use in mind, there could be value with this offer. Do you plan on buying American miles with this promotion?

title: Kimpton Social Password Winter 2026-2027: “This Calls For Something”
summary: Kimpton's social password for winter is "this calls for something," valid November 27, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Here's how it works and what I won at check-in.
content: Kimpton has a pretty cool “social password” concept, whereby you can receive extra perks for sharing a phrase at check-in. Kimpton generally has this promotion a couple of times per year — we last saw this in summer, and there’s now a new password for winter. I’d like to talk about what the new password is, share my experience using it, and also pose a question to Kimpton regulars about the least cringeworthy way to go about saying it. What is the current Kimpton password? Kimpton is one of the cooler IHG hotel groups, and there are a variety of things that set Kimpton apart from other IHG brands. One of those things is the social password. The idea is that seasonally, Kimpton provides a phrase through social media that you’re supposed to say when you check-in, and if you do that, you’ll receive something extra. The new Kimpton password is “this calls for something,” and it’s valid for stays between November 27, 2026, and February 28, 2027. So just say that when you check-in at a Kimpton property during the promotion period, and you’ll receive a surprise. My experience using the Kimpton password For those curious about what happens when you say the Kimpton password, I stayed at the Kimpton EPIC Miami some time back, which was my first Kimpton stay in quite a while (and I haven’t stayed at one since either). It was a good value as well , as I was able to use a free night award earned with the New IHG One Rewards Premier Credit Card ( learn more ). I was curious what the benefit would be for using the password. So I shared the password with the front desk agent. At the conclusion of the check-in experience, he brought out a game show-style wheel. I might have spun too hard, as it must have gone around for about 30 seconds. Go figure I landed on the tile that just had me spin again. Then I spun again, and the prize was free parking. I had a car and was staying for two nights, and parking costs $44 per night. So using the Kimpton password saved me nearly $100 — score!! Kimpton social password wheel Based on looking at the wheel, it seems that some of the other prizes include a free welcome drink, free breakfast, free snacks, and a free movie. There were also a few empty squares, where I guess you don’t win anything. And I’m not sure what the alarm clock, car tipping over, or postcard of Miami get you. Regardless, I’d say those are some awesome prizes, and I got a great reward. It’s cute how the Kimpton EPIC Miami makes a game of this. I know there’s a lot of inconsistency when it comes to this benefit across Kimpton properties. Some hotels provide meaningful perks (an upgrade, free, parking, etc.), like I got here, while other hotels provide a 19 cent branded koozie. It’s great that this has stuck around, given that it has presumably become increasingly popular. Years ago not everyone was on social media, so it was a good way to encourage people to follow Kimpton on X, Facebook, Instagram, etc. With the way the internet has evolved, times have changed a bit. How do you non-awkwardly say the Kimpton password? I’m sure I’m not the only one who finds the concept of saying a password at check-in to be kind of weird. So I think it’s fun to compare notes about how people share the password at the front desk. I find it awkward to just blurt out the password out of nowhere. So when I used this for my stay, I said “I guess I’m supposed to say [social password] as the social password?” That did the trick, but I’d be curious to hear how other Kimpton regulars go about this! Bottom line Between November 27, 2026, and February 28, 2027, Kimpton’s social password is “this calls for something.” Just state that phrase when you check-in at a Kimpton, and you should get some sort of a surprise. The gift will vary by property, so there’s no reason not to take advantage of this if staying at a Kimpton. The last time I used the password I got to spin a wheel at check-in, and then I ended up getting free parking, which was a value of $44 per night. If you’ve used the Kimpton password, what was your experience like?

title: Book A Southwest Airlines Ticket, Get Promotional Companion Pass
summary: Southwest Airlines has launched another Companion Pass promotion. Register, then book one roundtrip ticket between November 27 and 29, 2026, and you can earn a Companion Pass valid into early March 2027.
content: Southwest Airlines has just introduced an incredibly generous promotion, which we see several times per year. With this, you can earn a promotional Companion Pass after booking a single roundtrip ticket, and that could be a great deal. Book a ticket, get Companion Pass for several weeks With a new promotion from Southwest, you can earn a promotional Companion Pass by booking a single roundtrip ticket (or two one-ways). Here are the details of how this works: You must register for the promotion , and then purchase one roundtrip or two one-way tickets between November 27 and November 29, 2026 (yes, the ticket has to be booked after registering, so it’s a short booking window; however, you can always cancel an existing ticket and rebook with vouchers) In order for a ticket to qualify, it can be booked with cash, points, or Cash + Points You must travel by January 5, 2027 Then you can earn a promotional Companion Pass that’s valid for travel between January 8 and March 3, 2027; you’ll be able to change your companion up to three times during the promotion period This is an extremely generous offer. We usually see an offer like this a few times per year, so it’s nice to see it return. It seems that even with all the other changes at Southwest, this promotion is at least one thing that’s remaining consistent. There’s a great Southwest Companion Pass promo What is Southwest Airlines Companion Pass? For those of you not familiar with Companion Pass , it’s one of the best deals in travel. Those with Companion Pass can have a companion fly with them for just the cost of taxes, regardless of whether paying cash or redeeming points. Essentially think of it as a two-for-one travel pass, which is otherwise pretty unheard of. Under the current rules, Southwest Companion Pass ordinarily requires 100 flights or 135,000 qualifying points in a calendar year, so this promotion offers quite the shortcut (though also with a limited travel window). We are seeing changes to Companion Pass in 2027 , as Companion Pass will become a perk of top tier Platinum elite status, rather than something that’s separately qualified for. Earn a limited time Companion Pass with this promotion Bottom line Southwest Airlines has introduced a generous promotion that can earn you Companion Pass. Those who register and then book a roundtrip ticket between November 27 and November 29, 2026, for travel by January 5, 2027, can earn a promotional Companion Pass valid for several weeks early next year. Obviously this promotion isn’t for everyone, but if you have any travel to potentially plan over the promotion period, then this offer is seriously worth considering. It’s awesome how often Southwest offers this promotion. Do you plan on taking advantage of this Southwest Companion Pass promo?

title: Ryanair Now Withholds Free Seats Until Just Before Departure, Blames Customer Feedback
summary: Ryanair now holds back free random seat assignments until three to four hours before departure, citing customer feedback. The likelier goal is getting more passengers to pay for seats.
content: Ryanair has quietly updated its policy for how it assigns seats to those people who don’t pay the seat assignment fee, as reported by The Irish Times . While I wouldn’t consider this to be anything unreasonable, what I’m amused by is the carrier’s justification. The airline claims that it’s doing this due to customer feedback, rather than to generate more revenue. Ryanair now only allocates seats closer to departure Ryanair is known for being an unapologetic ultra low cost carrier. The airline has low base fares, and then charges fees for just about everything. Among other things, the airline charges to assign seats in advance, and those who don’t pay for specific seat assignments are just randomly assigned seats (and often in a rather punitive way). However, the way the airline is randomly allocating seats has quietly changed as of late October 2026, coinciding with the start of the winter schedule. Historically, the airline has automatically assigned seats to passengers without seat assignments around 24 hours before departure. Some passengers seemed to “game” this, and would essentially “gamble.” What they’d do is wait until 24 hours out to see what seat they were assigned for free. Then if they weren’t happy with their automatic seat assignment, they could still pay to assign a better seat. Under the new policy, the airline still issues a boarding pass up to 24 hours out, but without a seat assignment. Then the boarding pass automatically shows the seat assignment within four hours of departure. The logic here seems pretty clear — some people do care somewhat about where they sit, but want to avoid fees if they can. By withholding seat assignments until hours before departure, passengers are presumably more likely to pay for seat assignments in advance, to avoid that uncertainty. Ryanair has a new approach for seat allocations Ryanair spins this policy change as a positive Ryanair has confirmed this seat assignment policy change in a statement, sharing that “the timing of the allocation of free random seats is determined at all times by the airline.” Right, nobody disputes that the airline has the right to do this. So, what’s the logic for this policy change? According to the airline, it’s “to allow those passengers who wish to select their preferred seat more time to do so. We had a number of complaints this summer that passengers could not book their preferred seat on the day of travel as it had been already randomly allocated as a free seat up to 24 hours prior to departure.” The Ryanair representative went on to say that “passengers who choose a free of charge random seat clearly don’t mind where they sit, and their digital boarding pass is automatically updated between three to four hours prior to departure, which is well before they arrive at either their departure airport or their boarding gate.” Ryanair is of course within its rights to have this policy, but I think the logic is pretty obvious, and it’s to generate more revenue. After all, 24 hours out people would see what they were randomly assigned at online check-in, and would still have a lot of choices if they wanted to pay for seats, since most people don’t check-in online exactly at the 24-hour mark. But within a few hours of departure, virtually everyone has checked in online, and not many seats will be left. So I imagine the goal is to condition more customers to pay for seat assignments in advance. I love the claim that customers complained that their preferred seats on the day of travel were randomly allocated to others for free: Why didn’t those people who wanted to pay for seats assign them further in advance? Does Ryanair have that many same day bookings? How do the customers known that those seats were assigned to others for free, rather than to others who were paying? Ryanair presumably wants more people paying for seats Bottom line Ryanair has a new policy for automatic seat allocations. In the past, the airline would automatically assign seats to passengers 24 hours out, giving them quite the window to “gamble” on the free seat assignment, and then pay for a different seat assignment if they weren’t happy with the free one. The airline has now started only assigning free seats at most four hours out. The airline claims that this is due to customer feedback, so that passengers have more time to assign their choice of paid seats. However, I imagine that’s not quite accurate, and this is instead about conditioning people to pay for seat assignments, rather than “gambling” on the free allocations. What do you make of this Ryanair seating policy change?

title: Citi AAdvantage Executive Card Review: Is The Admirals Club Perk Worth It?
summary: A full breakdown of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card's welcome bonus, Admirals Club membership, elite status earning potential, and other card perks.
content: The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (formerly known as the Citi AAdvantage Executive World Elite Mastercard) is American Airlines’ most premium co-branded credit card, as part of the Citi partnership . While the Citi AA Executive Card has a steep annual fee, it offers strong perks, ranging from an Admirals Club membership, to the ability to supercharge your AAdvantage elite status, to credits that can help offset the annual fee. If you ask me, it’s one of the best value premium airline credit cards out there, and it’s also the airline credit card with the strongest lounge access perks. While products like the American Express Platinum Card® ( learn more ) and Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card ( learn more ) might typically be the first that come to mind when people consider premium cards, this one could make a lot more sense if you’re a frequent American flyer. In this post, I’d like to take an in-depth look at the Citi AA Executive Card, with my Citi AAdvantage Executive Card review. I think this is especially important in light of the card’s recent refresh , where we saw the annual fee increase, but also saw new perks added. Link: Learn more about the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® Citi AAdvantage Executive Card summary & key details Let me start by briefly summarizing the key details of the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card : Citi AA Executive Card annual fee : $695 Citi AA Executive Card authorized user fee : $175 for up to three authorized users, then $175 per additional authorized user after that Citi AA Executive Card welcome bonus : 80,000 miles after spending $8,000 within the first three months Citi AA Executive Card rewards : 12x miles on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and Cars bookings, 4x miles on eligible American Airlines purchases, and 1x miles on other purchases Citi AA Executive Card Loyalty Points : Earn 1x Loyalty Points per eligible dollar spent, plus up to 40K bonus Loyalty Points per year for passing certain thresholds Citi AA Executive Card foreign transaction fees : none Citi AA Executive Card Admirals Club access : Admirals Club access for the primary cardmember and authorized users Citi AA Executive Card first checked bag : first checked bag free on eligible American Airlines domestic itineraries for the cardmember and up to eight companions on the same reservation Citi AA Executive Card priority benefits : priority check-in, priority screening where available, and Group 4 boarding on eligible American Airlines flights Citi AA Executive Card American Airlines Vacations credits : up to $500 toward eligible American Airlines Vacations purchases annually Citi AA Executive Card InKind credits : up to $200 per year in InKind credits, as a $100 semi-annual credit Citi AA Executive Card Lyft credits : up to $15 per month in Lyft credits, after taking three rides Citi AA Executive Card Avis/Budget credits : up to $120 back per year on eligible prepaid Avis or Budget rentals Citi AA Executive Card inflight & Admirals Club credits : up to $100 per year toward eligible American Airlines inflight or Admirals Club purchases Citi AA Executive Card Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credits : up to $120 statement credits for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck once every four years This is the ideal card if you value American Admirals Club lounge access, if you’re going for elite status with American AAdvantage, or if you can just make the credits on the card work. If you’re just an occasional American flyer, there are probably more affordable options that will be easier to justify in the long term. However, with the card’s big welcome bonus, there’s a huge incentive to give this card a try. The Citi Executive Card is American’s most premium product Citi AAdvantage Executive Card bonus, fee, rewards One of the reasons that you’ll want to consider applying for the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card is because of the excellent welcome bonus it has. Of course that has to be balanced with the annual fee, and you also have to take into account the eligibility requirements, so let’s go through those details for the Citi AA Executive Card. Welcome bonus of 80,000 AAdvantage miles The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card currently has a welcome bonus of 80,000 AAdvantage bonus miles after spending $8,000 within the first three months. Personally, I value American AAdvantage miles at ~1.5 cents each, so to me, those miles are worth about $1,200. That’s an excellent bonus, especially for a card that also offers a lot of value in the long run. There are so many great uses of AAdvantage miles , including for travel on partner airlines. For what it’s worth, I value Delta SkyMiles at 1.1 cents each, and United MileagePlus miles at 1.3 cents each, so these are the most valuable miles among the “big three” carriers, based on my math. Redeem American AAdvantage miles for Etihad first class Card bonus & eligibility rules The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card bonus miles aren’t available to those who have received a new cardmember bonus for this card in the past 48 months (however, you are eligible if you’ve had a different American Airlines credit card, including if you’ve received a bonus on a different product). Then there are the typical rules for Citi credit card applications , including that you can apply for at most one card with Citi every eight days, and at most two cards every 65 days. There’s not a consistent credit score that you need to get approved for the card, though I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that determines eligibility. Annual fee & authorized user fee The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has a $695 annual fee. There’s also a lot of value to adding authorized users (as I’ll discuss below). You can expect to pay a total of $175 for up to three authorized users (so potentially under $60 each), and then each authorized user after that costs $175. Keep in mind that if you’re a Citigold customer , you can receive a $145 annual rebate on your annual fee, which is a nice perk. Rewards structure & earning Loyalty Points When it comes to spending money on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card , here’s the rewards structure: Earn 12x AAdvantage miles on eligible rental cars booked through aa.com/cars, and eligible hotels booked through aa.com/hotels Earn 4x AAdvantage miles on eligible American Airlines purchases; furthermore, after spending $150,000 on the card in a calendar year, cardmembers can earn a total of 5x AAdvantage miles on eligible American Airlines purchases for the remainder of the calendar year Earn 1x AAdvantage miles on all other purchases In terms of the reward for spending, there are potentially better cards for purchasing airline tickets , and also better cards for everyday spending . However, keep in mind that the most compelling reason to spend money on the card is in order to earn elite status with American Airlines. American Airlines uses its Loyalty Points system for status qualification, and credit card spending can help you earn status . American’s elite requirements are currently as follows, and you earn one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on an American Airlines credit card: AAdvantage Gold status requires 40,000 Loyalty Points AAdvantage Platinum status requires 75,000 Loyalty Points AAdvantage Platinum Pro status requires 125,000 Loyalty Points AAdvantage Executive Platinum status requires 200,000 Loyalty Points Spending on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card could earn you elite status, which I know will interest many. That’s the primary reason you’ll want to consider this card for spending. I do want to specifically point out one thing that throws people off — you earn one Loyalty Point per dollar spent on the card, unrelated to how many miles you earn for spending. In other words, if you’re making an American Airlines purchase, you’d earn 4x AAdvantage redeemable miles, but only 1x Loyalty Points on the purchase as such. Spend your way to elite status with AAdvantage credit cards Earn up to 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points In addition to earning one Loyalty Point for every dollar spent on the Citi AAdvantage Executive Card, you can also earn up to 40,000 Loyalty Points every year just for being a cardmember: Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 50,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 90,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 165,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year Earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points when you earn 240,000 Loyalty Points with AAdvantage in a status qualification year In other words, if you have this card, you’d only otherwise need to earn 170,000 Loyalty Points for Executive Platinum status, since this card would get you a boost of 30,000 Loyalty Points at that level. Those Loyalty Points can be earned in a variety of ways, ranging from flying, to online shopping, to credit card spending, to booking vacation packages. Either way, this Loyalty Points boost would be quite the advantage in terms of qualifying for Loyalty Point Rewards , and even upgrade priority . The AAdvantage elite qualifying year goes from the beginning of March until the end of February of the following year. You don’t need to have the card at the beginning of the year to take advantage of this, so even if you open the card during the membership year, you could still earn 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points for that year (in other words, the credits can be retroactive). Access Flagship Lounges with AAdvantage elite status No foreign transaction fees The Citi AAdvantage Executive Card has no foreign transaction fees, so this can be a good option for purchases abroad .
